summary: Raman alone cannot establish that flake 2 is a monolayer. What the data do show: flake 2's E2g band is about 10% as intense as flake 1's (area ratio 0.10; 0.08–0.13 across fit choices), its E2g center is blueshifted by +2.8 cm-1 (1369.0 vs 1366.2), and it is broader (FWHM 21–22 vs 18 cm-1). Taken at face value, flake 2 is much thinner than flake 1. If E2g intensity scales linearly with thickness (valid for hBN below ~3 nm in my thin-film model), flake 2 is about 0.1 times flake 1's thickness. That makes it monolayer only if flake 1 is about 3 nm (~10 layers). The Si-band ratio (18.8x) cannot be produced by hBN thickness on this stack in my model (max ~5x over 0–300 nm), so it reflects focus, coverage or substrate differences, not layer number. The layer number therefore needs AFM on both flakes, or a reference of known thickness measured under identical conditions.

observations.finding: Flake 1 E2g is at 1366.20 cm-1, bulk-like, with FWHM 17.9 cm-1 and peak SNR about 80.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian + quadratic baseline fit over 1320–1410 cm-1. Center 1366.20 ± 0.04 cm-1 (residual bootstrap, 200 resamples). Residual sigma 40.5 counts. Si first-order band at 520.91 cm-1 (FWHM 3.4 cm-1).

observations.finding: Flake 2 E2g is blueshifted by about +2.8 cm-1 relative to flake 1 and is broader.
observations.evidence: Center 1368.97–1369.12 cm-1 across 6 window/baseline choices; bootstrap sd 0.24 cm-1, 95% CI 1368.53–1369.43. FWHM 19.2–23.9 cm-1 across choices (about 21–22 typical), vs 17.9 for flake 1. Si band at 520.90 cm-1 in both spectra, so there is no calibration offset between the spectra. The E2g line is much broader than the Si line (3.4–3.5 cm-1), so the broadening is intrinsic to the hBN, not instrumental.

observations.finding: Flake 2 E2g integrated intensity is about 10% of flake 1's.
observations.evidence: Area ratio flake2/flake1 = 0.102 (fit with quadratic baseline over 1300–1430 cm-1 gives 0.097; linear baseline gives 0.106). Range across 8 window/baseline choices: 0.079–0.130, median 0.099. Peak SNR for flake 2 is about 14 (height 261 counts over a 1570-count background, residual sigma 19 counts).

observations.finding: The Si 520 cm-1 band is about 19x stronger in flake 2 than in flake 1, but hBN thickness cannot plausibly produce that.
observations.evidence: Si area 311,205 (flake 2) vs 16,591 (flake 1), ratio 18.8. My thin-film model (air | hBN | 290 nm SiO2 | Si, 514.5 nm, normal incidence) gives Si signal relative to bare SiO2 between 0.22 and 1.17 over 0–300 nm of hBN, so the maximum achievable Si ratio is about 5.4x. No thickness pair matches both the Si ratio (18.8) and the E2g ratio (0.10); the best fit gives a Si ratio of 4.3.

observations.finding: Within a thin-film optical model, E2g yield per unit thickness is linear up to about 3 nm, so E2g intensity scales with layer number in that regime.
observations.evidence: Normalized E2g yield per nm: 1.00 (0.335 nm), 0.989 (0.67 nm), 0.978 (1 nm), 0.944 (2 nm), 0.908 (3 nm), 0.833 (5 nm), 0.645 (10 nm), 0.35 (20 nm), 0.08 (50 nm). Interference suppresses yield for thicker flakes. Si signal changes by under 10% for thicknesses up to 3 nm.

observations.finding: Flake 2 has an elevated continuum background.
observations.evidence: Median counts 1670 (flake 2) vs 1003 (flake 1). Background under the E2g band is about 1570 (flake 2) vs about 1150 (flake 1). Noise is about 19 counts point-to-point (flake 2) vs about 42 (flake 1), so the background is not simply higher noise.

observations.finding: Flake 1 has several weak features (493, 787, 907, 979, 1230, 1473 cm-1) at about 2 sigma. The 493 cm-1 feature could be the SiO2 D1 defect band, but it is marginal.
observations.evidence: Prominences 75–118 counts vs point-to-point noise of about 42 counts. None of these are hBN first-order modes, and they are not analysed further.

properties.name: layers
properties.value: Not determined. Flake 2 is thinner than flake 1 by roughly 10x in E2g intensity. Monolayer is consistent only if flake 1 is about 3.3 nm (~10 layers); if flake 1 is 10 nm, flake 2 is about 3 layers.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: Not established. Broader E2g (21–22 vs 18 cm-1) weakly suggests more disorder or strain in flake 2, but the difference is only about 4 cm-1 and the fit uncertainty is small, so it could reflect a different model rather than a real change.

properties.name: L_D_nm
properties.value: not applicable (no graphene D band in hBN spectra)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: undetermined. The +2.8 cm-1 E2g upshift is consistent with compressive strain or thinning, but these cannot be separated from one spectrum.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.value: none assessable from hBN (insulator, E2g not a doping probe at this level)

properties.name: phase
properties.value: hexagonal BN (single E2g mode in range)

caveats: The E2g area ratio (about 0.10) assumes the same laser spot coverage and focus on both flakes. The large Si-band difference (19x) suggests focus, spot coverage or substrate differences exist; if flake 2 covers only part of the spot, its E2g intensity is underestimated and the thickness inference is biased thin.

The thin-film model uses assumed indices (hBN n=2.1 at 514.5 nm, SiO2 n=1.46, Si 4.3+0.05i), normal incidence, no objective NA or collection-geometry effects, and uniform Raman yield. The qualitative conclusion (Si ratio cannot reach 19x from thickness) is robust to moderate index changes; the quantitative E2g-vs-thickness curve is not validated.
The linear-thickness scaling of E2g and the 10% thickness ratio only hold below about 3 nm in this model. For a monolayer-vs-bulk question the flake 1 thickness is critical and unknown.
The E2g shift of +2.8 cm-1 could come from thinning, strain, substrate or interface effects, or defects. The Si calibration agrees between spectra, so instrumental calibration is not the explanation.
Laser heating would redshift E2g, not blueshift it, and hBN is transparent at 514.5 nm, so heating is an unlikely explanation for the difference.
Flake 1 E2g at 1366.2 cm-1 suggests bulk-like but does not prove flake 1 is thick.

FWHM of 18–22 cm-1 is broad compared with reports for high-quality bulk hBN (about 7–10 cm-1 from memory); this may indicate disorder or non-ideal sample or spectral resolution, but the Si line (3.4 cm-1) shows instrument resolution is fine.
questions_for_user: What is flake 1's thickness (AFM step height)? This sets the absolute layer number of flake 2; without it the Raman result is only relative.
Is there an AFM height profile across flake 2 (ideally including an edge to bare SiO2)? A 0.33 nm step per layer is measurable by AFM and is the decisive test for a monolayer.
What were the laser power at the sample, objective NA, spot size and grating/resolution? These bear on the intensity comparison and on whether the same spot coverage applies.
Was the same spot and focus used on both flakes? Was the Si substrate reference measured on bare SiO2 nearby? The Si-band difference (19x) needs explaining before intensities are used quantitatively.
Why is the continuum background elevated in flake 2 (about 1500–1700 vs 370–1150 counts)? Is there fluorescence, residue, or a dark-offset or acquisition difference between the two spectra?
Are the flakes exfoliated from the same bulk crystal, and was flake 2 annealed or processed? Residue or strain could explain the blueshift and broadening.
Could you map E2g intensity and position across flake 2 (and an area of flake 1 at a known thickness) to check uniformity and edges?
